_text_key: over 24 weeks labour induction — looking for advice :) || hi everyone, i recently found out i am 25 weeks and 5 days pregnant as of today, which was a total shock to me as i’ve had no symptoms and my stomach at most looks like i’m just bloated. i didn’t get my period because of my birth control so i had no way of really knowing and after having not even a scare for 8 years of being on said birth control i truly thought i was in the clear. hearing i was 25 weeks and unfortunately past the cut off gestation for a d&e in vancouver b.c where i live was absolutely terrifying, but the b.c women’s hospital’s care centre reached out to me and let me know they can perform a labour induction here in vancouver up to 28 weeks, and so they are working on getting me an appointment. i haven’t received a call yet as they said this takes some time so i’m a bit anxious waiting as i’d love to have the appointment date set for peace of mind, but i was wondering if anyone has found themselves in a similar situation and how the experience was with the labour induction method of terminating? they did their best to explain to me what to expect but i was in such a state of shock and anxiety it was hard to absorb all of the information. additionally, to anyone who may be in a similar circumstance you are not alone!! it may feel hopeless to hear that you are past the gestation date for a typical d&e abortion, but there are always options and resources for you, even if it feels too late and hopeless. i hope my experience can bring a bit of comfort to anyone who finds out at 25 weeks or more and are feeling like they don’t have any options.

Additionally, to anyone who may be in a similar circumstance you are not alone!! I hope my experience can bring a bit of comfort to anyone who finds out at 25 weeks or more and are feeling like they don’t have any options.

_text_key: miscarried naturally at 14 weeks. what to do next ? || my 8 weeks scan looked good but i had started light spotting at 10w5d. i had an ultrasound done the very next day and we could see fetal movement. obgyn reassured that spotting is not uncommon in pregnancy. jump to 13w2d: i had my mfm(maternal fetal medicine) 1st trimester scan and i was still spotting. we saw a normal heartbeat of 155 bpm. baby had developed arms and legs but it showed a gestational age of 11w3d based on the fetus size. mfm specialist was concerned that either it meant an abnormality in fetal growth, or an impending miscarriage or some measurement error. i was told to come back for another scan in 2 weeks to check back on the fetal size. six days passed and on saturday (14w): i started experiencing more period like bleeding. i waited for a day and we went to the er the next day. sunday(14w1d): the on-call doctor in er did a scan and found out there was no fetal heartbeat. my hcg levels were also low. the fetal size that day was supposedly same as that of a 10 or 11 weeks fetus. er doctor finally revealed the news that i was in the middle of a miscarriage and i might experience heavy bleeding in couple of days. i was so disheartened and didn't know what to do. me and my husband were in shock and we couldn't think properly to ask him enough questions like the risk associated with at home natural miscarriage, the process to properly collect and store fetal tissue to send it for further testing, and whether we should consider d&c as i was at 14 weeks(almost into 2nd trimester) even though the fetal size was small (10 or 11 weeks) he mentioned i might pass along lot of clots and will experience heavy bleeding and the fetal tissue should pass along with it. that night i also contacted my obgyn and updated him about the status, however he was on leave and unable to provide any care that weekend and a day after that. i slept out that night. monday(14w2d): the next day seemed bearable as well as i did not experience any cramps or pain other than mild bleeding. but as the night approached, the horror began. i started to feel super uneasy. i felt super nauseous and had to vomit 4 to 5 times. i also felt the urge to poop and went twice. my bleeding had increased significantly and i was changing pads every hour. this was going on for couple of hours, and then the moment came. i had gotten up from bed to puke again and i experienced a big clot coming out of my vagina and i knew my pad was unable to handle such a big clot so i immediately went to the toilet. i had kind of gotten an idea that this might be it. and so it was, i passed the fetal tissue and it was a small fetus(approx 4-5cm). my heart sank and didn't know what to do. it happened so fast that we didn't think that we could collect it(and how?), store it in a sterile container to take it to a lab the next day for further testing. after passing of the fetal tissue i suddenly felt a relief and my pain subsided a little however i was still bleeding heavily. tuesday: the next day my obgyn was back and i got an urgent appointment with him. he checked my cervix and mentioned that it was closed. he also did an abdominal ultrasound scan and didn't see any remaining tissue. he mentioned that if i experience heavy bleeding even after 2-3 weeks then i should go to er to get a d&c done. i asked him if we should schedule one with him just to confirm everything but he seemed pretty confident on the ultrasound results that there was no tissue left. i am still worried if everything would have come off as i was almost into the 2nd trimester. i know d&c will also need some healing afterwards as well. should i follow my obgyn's instructions or urge him to do a d&c just to check everything once ? any advice will be helpful. thank you!

body:
My 8 weeks scan looked good but I had started light spotting at 10w5d. I had an ultrasound done the very next day and we could see fetal movement. OBGYN reassured that spotting is not uncommon in pregnancy.

Jump to 13w2d:  I had my MFM(Maternal Fetal Medicine) 1st trimester scan and I was still spotting. We saw a normal heartbeat of 155 bpm. Baby had developed arms and legs but it showed a gestational age of 11w3d based on the fetus size. MFM specialist was concerned that either it meant an abnormality in fetal growth, or an impending miscarriage or some measurement error. I was told to come back for another scan in 2 weeks to check back on the fetal size. 

Six days passed and on Saturday (14w): I started experiencing more period like bleeding. I waited for a day and we went to the ER the next day. 

Sunday(14w1d):  
The on-call doctor in ER did a scan and found out there was no fetal heartbeat. My HCG levels were also low.  The fetal size that day was supposedly same as that of a 10 or 11 weeks fetus.

ER doctor finally revealed the news that I was in the middle of a miscarriage and I might experience heavy bleeding in couple of days. 

I was so disheartened and didn't know what to do. Me and my husband were in shock and we couldn't think properly to ask him enough questions like the risk associated with at home natural miscarriage, the process to properly collect and store fetal tissue to send it for further testing, and whether we should consider D&C as I was at 14 weeks(almost into 2nd trimester) even though the fetal size was small (10 or 11 weeks)

He mentioned I might pass along lot of clots and will experience heavy bleeding and the fetal tissue should pass along with it. 

That night I also contacted my Obgyn and updated him about the status, however he was on leave and unable to provide any care that weekend and a day after that. 

I slept out that night. 

Monday(14w2d): 
The next day seemed bearable as well as I did not experience any cramps or pain other than mild bleeding. 

But as the night approached, the horror began. I started to feel super uneasy. I felt super nauseous and had to vomit 4 to 5 times. I also felt the urge to poop and went twice. My bleeding had increased significantly and I was changing pads every hour.

This was going on for couple of hours, and then the moment came. I had gotten up from bed to puke again and I experienced a big clot coming out of my vagina and I knew my pad was unable to handle such a big clot so I immediately went to the toilet. I had kind of gotten an idea that this might be it. 

And so it was, I passed the fetal tissue and it was a small fetus(approx 4-5cm). My heart sank and didn't know what to do. It happened so fast that we didn't think that we could collect it(and how?), store it in a sterile container to take it to a lab the next day for further testing. 

After passing of the fetal tissue I suddenly felt a relief and my pain subsided a little however I was still bleeding heavily.

Tuesday:
The next day my Obgyn was back and I got an urgent appointment with him. He checked my cervix and mentioned that it was closed. He also did an abdominal ultrasound scan and didn't see any remaining tissue. He mentioned that if I experience heavy bleeding even after 2-3 weeks then I should go to ER to get a D&C done. 

I asked him if we should schedule one with him just to confirm everything but he seemed pretty confident on the ultrasound results that there was no tissue left. 

I am still worried if everything would have come off as I was almost into the 2nd trimester. I know D&C will also need some healing afterwards as well.

Should I follow my Obgyn's instructions or urge him to do a D&C just to check everything once ? 


Any advice will be helpful. Thank you!

_text_key: my experience (2 rounds of cytotec and a d&c) || i found out i had a miscarriage at my 9 week appointment, the baby was measuring 6 weeks 5 days and had no heartbeat. i was allowed to wait a week for a second ultrasound to see if maybe i had just ovulated late or something. spoiler- i didn't. (extra tw for this paragraph - it's kind of graphic) >!the second scan was honestly scarring and i don't know if i'll ever be able to forget seeing the fragments of what was left of my baby as it was reabsorbed into my body/the sac.!< the following week they allowed me to wait another week (so 2 full weeks of knowing about the miscarriage but doing nothing but waiting). after that they suggested either a d&c or to take misoprostal. i opted for the latter because i'm still breastfeeding my firstborn child and i was scared of the d&c. i took it vaginally the first time, two doses 24 hours apart. i cramped and bled and the whole nine yards but went back for a follow up to find out that nothing had happened. the second round i took orally, two doses 24 hours apart. this was a week after the first round. almost nothing happened aside from some light bleeding and cramping. at the follow up appointment i knew what they would say because there was no way it worked. i just had a d&c today and i don't know how to feel. it has been 6 weeks since i found out i lost my baby and it feels like i've been living in limbo. i'm trying to be grateful and present for my firstborn baby but it's hard knowing what could've been. to add salt to the wound, when they were wheeling me to the recovery room the first thing i saw was a mural on the wall of a mommy bird feeding two baby birds and instantly teared up. i don't know why i'm sharing this. i didn't tell any of my family about this because i'm weird and didn't know how. i do have my (very supportive) boyfriend and a friend who i can confide in but it feels so isolating. if you read all this, thanks for reading my mouth diarrhea lol. my heart goes out to everyone who's a part of this horrible "club".

_text_key: encouragement post || i wanted to briefly share my experience, in hopes it might help encourage someone else now or sometime in the future. i recently experienced my first miscarriage, a mmc. we had our first ultrasound at 9 weeks, 3 days. our little one was only measuring 7 weeks and 3 days. there was no heart beat. obviously we were so sad about this news. that appointment was a blur, and just basically by default, i chose the option of expectant management. i wanted time to process my emotions, and i knew i could always make a different decision if needed. i guess deep down, i also still held out some hope maybe they were wrong and everything would be ok. i realize that was just part of trying to process the grief. i scheduled another appointment for two weeks later and went home to wait. those two weeks were two of the most difficult weeks of my life. the waiting, the fear of how and when things would start, fear of being to far away from home, just in case. every time i looked down, i knew our baby was still with me, but no longer developing or growing. it was just a very difficult time. i had lots of cramping, but no spotting. i kept thinking, "this is it, it's starting", but it didn't. that was also very frustrating to go from praying you don't start spotting when you think your baby is still healthy and growing, to being disappointed you're not spotting because you just want to get the process over with. i went to my appointment after the two weeks. i discussed everything with the doctor, and also mentioned we had a short weekend trip coming up that i was really thinking of canceling because i was worried about the process beginning while out of town. she listened intently, the basically just said, "i think given everything i'm hearing you say, and the fact that it's been 4 weeks since the baby passed, your best option would be a d&c. why don't we schedule it for thursday?" that was only 2 days later. immediately when she said that, i felt like 1000 pounds were lifted off my shoulders and the noise that had been constant in my head and heart since we received the news about our baby finally calmed. i knew right away, even though i hadn't truly considered this option previously, that it was the right thing to do. we scheduled the procedure. the night before the procedure, i started to spot. i was so upset because i literally only had to get through one more night, and my body couldn't even do that right. i called the after hours nurses line, and they told me what to watch out for, but said to come in for my procedure anyway, no matter what, so they could monitor me and make sure the process was complete. i had my procedure this morning, and for the first time during this whole ordeal, i finally feel some peace. of course i wish things were different, but this was a merciful end to so much suffering. everything went smoothly and i was only at the hospital for about 2 hours. i had no nausea after and so far, no pain. bleeding is like a light period. i guess i just wanted to share because i was so conflicted about having this done when given the 3 options at our ultrasound. i really like to let my body do its thing, and i don't like to use medical intervention or any medication unless absolutely necessary. but truly, this was the best decision i could have made. i wasn't honoring our baby by continuing to wait. there is no prize for suffering, and no shame in needing closure. i know i can begin to heal now in all ways because i no longer have to worry about myself or my health and safety. i definitely don't mean to say this is best for everyone. everyone deserves the chance to work through this horrible situation however they need to. but for me, i needed to be able to begin to truly move on and work through the grief. so even if you are committed to a particular choice and change your mind, just know that it's absolutely your right to do that. edit to add: i completely understand i'm coming from a place of blessing that i was able to have this procedure with my medical coverage. i truly don't mean to marginalize anyone who isn't able to have this procedure due to cost or access. i simply wanted to share my experience for anyone on the fence, wanting to possibly go the route of having some kind of intervention, but very unsure or nervous about it. i'm terrified of anesthesia, i struggle with anxiety, and have several medication related allergies and reactions. i discussed the concerns with the anesthesiologist, and all was well. also, i really did struggle with the decision at times. anyone who has had to carry their baby after a mmc for any length of time understands the complexity of that experience. the tension between wanting to keep your baby with you, and protect them, while still understanding that at some point, you have to make a decision because you could become very sick or lose your life if it continues. it's a very difficult place to be. but ultimately, i knew my baby's little spirit would always be with me, and whatever state her little body was in after all that time wasn't honoring her anyway. we love her, and always will. i finally just had to tell her i was so sorry, but i had to stay healthy for her siblings, so that's why i had to make the decision to help my body along. i felt at peace that she understood, and knows how hard my body fought for weeks to protect her. whatever you choose, or however you must endure, i send you strength and love.
title: Encouragement post
body:
I wanted to briefly share my experience, in hopes it might help encourage someone else now or sometime in the future. 

I recently experienced my first miscarriage, a MMC. We had our first ultrasound at 9 weeks, 3 days. Our little one was only measuring 7 weeks and 3 days. There was no heart beat. 

Obviously we were so sad about this news. That appointment was a blur, and just basically by default, I chose the option of expectant management. I wanted time to process my emotions, and I knew I could always make a different decision if needed. I guess deep down, I also still held out some hope maybe they were wrong and everything would be ok. I realize that was just part of trying to process the grief. 

I scheduled another appointment for two weeks later and went home to wait. Those two weeks were two of the most difficult weeks of my life. The waiting, the fear of how and when things would start, fear of being to far away from home, just in case. Every time I looked down, I knew our baby was still with me, but no longer developing or growing. It was just a very difficult time. I had lots of cramping, but no spotting. I kept thinking, "this is it, it's starting", but it didn't. That was also very frustrating to go from praying you don't start spotting when you think your baby is still healthy and growing, to being disappointed you're not spotting because you just want to get the process over with. 

I went to my appointment after the two weeks. I discussed everything with the doctor, and also mentioned we had a short weekend trip coming up that I was really thinking of canceling because I was worried about the process beginning while out of town. She listened intently, the basically just said, "I think given everything I'm hearing you say, and the fact that it's been 4 weeks since the baby passed, your best option would be a D&C. Why don't we schedule it for Thursday?" That was only 2 days later. Immediately when she said that, I felt like 1000 pounds were lifted off my shoulders and the noise that had been constant in my head and heart since we received the news about our baby finally calmed. I knew right away, even though I hadn't truly considered this option previously, that it was the right thing to do. We scheduled the procedure. 

The night before the procedure, I started to spot. I was so upset because I literally only had to get through one more night, and my body couldn't even do that right. I called the after hours nurses line, and they told me what to watch out for, but said to come in for my procedure anyway, no matter what, so they could monitor me and make sure the process was complete. 

I had my procedure this morning, and for the first time during this whole ordeal, I finally feel some peace. Of course I wish things were different, but this was a merciful end to so much suffering. Everything went smoothly and I was only at the hospital for about 2 hours. I had no nausea after and so far, no pain. Bleeding is like a light period. 

I guess I just wanted to share because I was so conflicted about having this done when given the 3 options at our ultrasound. I really like to let my body do its thing, and I don't like to use medical intervention or any medication unless absolutely necessary. But truly, this was the best decision I could have made. I wasn't honoring our baby by continuing to wait. There is no prize for suffering, and no shame in needing closure. I know I can begin to heal now in all ways because I no longer have to worry about myself or my health and safety. 

I definitely don't mean to say this is best for everyone. Everyone deserves the chance to work through this horrible situation however they need to. But for me, I needed to be able to begin to truly move on and work through the grief. So even if you are committed to a particular choice and change your mind, just know that it's absolutely your right to do that. 

Edit to add: I completely understand I'm coming from a place of blessing that I was able to have this procedure with my medical coverage. I truly don't mean to marginalize anyone who isn't able to have this procedure due to cost or access. I simply wanted to share my experience for anyone on the fence, wanting to possibly go the route of having some kind of intervention, but very unsure or nervous about it. 

I'm terrified of anesthesia, I struggle with anxiety, and have several medication related allergies and reactions. I discussed the concerns with the anesthesiologist, and all was well. 

Also, I really did struggle with the decision at times. Anyone who has had to carry their baby after a MMC for any length of time understands the complexity of that experience. The tension between wanting to keep your baby with you, and protect them, while still understanding that at some point, you have to make a decision because you could become very sick or lose your life if it continues. It's a very difficult place to be. But ultimately, I knew my baby's little spirit would always be with me, and whatever state her little body was in after all that time wasn't honoring her anyway. We love her, and always will. I finally just had to tell her I was so sorry, but I had to stay healthy for her siblings, so that's why I had to make the decision to help my body along. I felt at peace that she understood, and knows how hard my body fought for weeks to protect her. 

Whatever you choose, or however you must endure, I send you strength and love.

_text_key: how do you cope with the “what-ifs”? || i’m 28 and had an abortion at 5 weeks last september… i was initially terrified when i found out about the pregnancy but started warming up to the idea once the shock settled. motherhood is something i’ve always wanted and still want, so even though it wasn’t planned, i was prepared to accept it and continue with the pregnancy… however, my partner was not on the same page. he felt that we weren’t in the best place financially (which granted we weren’t) but i still feel like we could have made it work if we really tried. i had a good amount saved up and he was finally getting settled in his career but he just wasn’t ready.. ultimately i decided to get the abortion because i didn’t want to bring my first child into the world with their father not fully onboard and excited for them. i felt quite numb in the early days and now i just have occasional, quiet moments of grief when i mourn what could have been. i wonder what the gender would have been, what they would have looked like and what kind of personality they would have had. all things that could only come from that specific egg and that specific sperm that i will never be able to recreate again. obviously i hope and plan to have children one day when we’re both ready but it kills me to think i will never know how that specific child would have turned out.. does anyone else feel this way?

title: Following the death of our child, my wife is pregnant again, I’m feeling deeply unsettled
body:
Last year, our little boy who was only two years old, passed away from an unexplained cardiac arrest. Do I even need to tell you how terrible and painful that was? In fact, it still is...

Two months ago, my wife and I decided that we wanted to have another child. She stopped her birth control, but shortly after, we became afraid that maybe we weren’t ready yet. Afraid that we weren’t stable enough.

But then...Surprise!...that small window of opportunity was enough for her to become pregnant. And we are both shaken by it. I say “we,” but from here on, I’ll speak for myself:

I’m scared. Scared of losing another child. Scared she might have a miscarriage, that something awful might happen again. Scared that I won’t be able to welcome this child with the joy they deserve. Because our first child was born in joy. Joy guided his life, we were such a very, very happy family... I’m scared of passing on my fear. Scared of not being ready. And above all, I’m scared of forgetting my son, of replacing him with new memories. I will never replace him...

I’m sad. Still grieving the death of my son, of course, but also sad because these small moments we’re living now remind me so much of those early days with him. I’m sad that he can’t be here to experience this with us. Sad that he will never meet his little brother or sister. Sad to see my wife cry when we should be feeling joy.

I’m happy. Happy to have had my son, he was the most wonderful little boy, and we spent all our time with him during those two years. We have no regrets. I’m happy to grow our family, to, in a way, give my son a little sibling who he’s watching over from above. I’m happy to become a father again. Happy, because I know this is what I want.

I’m tired. Tired of navigating all these emotions I just described. Sometimes I feel them all at once. When I walk into the room that used to be my son’s, I see the past, I see the future, I see the present... So much joy, fear, and sadness at the same time...

I wish I could feel only joy, but I just can’t, and I don’t know what to do to make it happen.

I’m writing these words because maybe other parents have been through this… How did you cope?  
My wife, who is currently pregnant, feels all of this, but even more intensely. I don’t know how to help her...

And also... I just... I just needed to write all this down somewhere. Maybe this post will vanish into the void, and that’s okay, it felt good to write it.

_text_key: and just like that, it’s over. || went in yesterday bright eyed and bushy tailed for my first appointment at 10 weeks. had my physical and my pap, all that good stuff. then, midwife wanted to do a dating scan. was excited for real ultrasound pics to take home to my husband and our 7 year old. ultrasound techs face was scrunched and i could already tell something was wrong. she clicked over to the setting that shows the heartbeat, and silence. she looked at me and said she was so sorry, that she was not seeing or hearing a heartbeat. the maternal-fetal medicine doc came in to verify. he couldn’t find anything either. just a silent baby shaped figure. they gave me condolences, my options, and ultimately i elected to do the misoprostol at home so that i could finish miscarrying in private. i know the statistics on miscarriages. i know how common it is. but for some reason i never considered it would be me. i’m angry and sad and confused all in one. then having to tell my son (who is constantly talking about “our baby”) that there is no more baby absolutely and utterly destroyed me. he was so heartbroken. leaving babybumps for a while. hopefully i can return in the future with a better story to share. hugs and love to all of you, especially the september 2023 crew. 🖤 *editing to update* - thank you all so much for the kind words and outpouring of love. i appreciate all of the kindness more than anyone can imagine. hopefully there will eventually be some light again after this dark time for our family.
title: And just like that, it’s over.
body:
Went in yesterday bright eyed and bushy tailed for my first appointment at 10 weeks. Had my physical and my pap, all that good stuff. Then, midwife wanted to do a dating scan. Was excited for real ultrasound pics to take home to my husband and our 7 year old. 

Ultrasound techs face was scrunched and I could already tell something was wrong. She clicked over to the setting that shows the heartbeat, and silence. She looked at me and said she was so sorry, that she was not seeing or hearing a heartbeat. The maternal-fetal medicine doc came in to verify. He couldn’t find anything either. Just a silent baby shaped figure. They gave me condolences, my options, and ultimately I elected to do the misoprostol at home so that I could finish miscarrying in private. 

I know the statistics on miscarriages. I know how common it is. But for some reason I never considered it would be me. I’m angry and sad and confused all in one. 

Then having to tell my son (who is CONSTANTLY talking about “our baby”) that there is no more baby absolutely and utterly destroyed me. He was so heartbroken. 

Leaving BabyBumps for a while. Hopefully I can return in the future with a better story to share. Hugs and love to all of you, especially the September 2023 crew.  🖤

*Editing to update* - thank you all so much for the kind words and outpouring of love. I appreciate all of the kindness more than anyone can imagine. Hopefully there will eventually be some light again after this dark time for our family.

_text_key: starting a card shop inventory saas (us + uk) — what data/privacy laws do i need to worry about? || hey all, i'm building a saas platform with a friend and could use some advice on the legal/data privacy side of things. here’s the situation: we’re in the early stages of launching a web-based inventory and order system for card shops with a android app.(think magic, pokémon, etc.). i’m based in missouri (u.s.), my co-founder is in the uk. the idea: shops pay a monthly subscription (via stripe) to use our service. we host their inventory and give them an in-store app. customers in the shop use a tablet to browse inventory, pick cards, enter their name, and submit an order. the shop fulfills the order using their own pos system (we don’t process payments from end-customers at all). each shop also gets a public-facing page where customers can pre-order cards online by entering name/email/phone. so far, we only plan to charge the card shops (not their customers). stripe handles subscription payments. my questions are: 1. since we’re collecting name/email/phone from end-users (card shop customers), are there specific data retention or privacy laws we need to follow? do we need to store this data for 7 years like financial records? can we just auto-delete it after, say, 90 days? 2. if an eu customer uses the platform (like a tourist or remote buyer), do we need to follow gdpr, even though we're u.s.-based? 3. do we need a data processing agreement (dpa) with each shop, since we’re acting as their data processor? 4. are there any special rules for stripe subscriptions we should keep in mind (ftc, refunds, disclosures)? 5. anything we’re likely to be missing here that’s easy to mess up? we're trying to do this right but keep it lightweight — especially since we’re not touching payment data from customers. would love to hear from anyone who’s done saas, worked with gdpr, or handled this kind of setup before. thanks in advance! location: missouri
title: Starting a Card Shop Inventory SaaS (US + UK) — What Data/Privacy Laws Do I Need to Worry About?

We’re in the early stages of launching a web-based inventory and order system for card shops with a android app.(think Magic, Pokémon, etc.). I’m based in Missouri (U.S.), my co-founder is in the UK. The idea:

Shops pay a monthly subscription (via Stripe) to use our service.

We host their inventory and give them an in-store app.

Customers in the shop use a tablet to browse inventory, pick cards, enter their name, and submit an order.

The shop fulfills the order using their own POS system (we don’t process payments from end-customers at all).

Each shop also gets a public-facing page where customers can pre-order cards online by entering name/email/phone.


So far, we only plan to charge the card shops (not their customers). Stripe handles subscription payments.

3. Do we need a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) with each shop, since we’re acting as their data processor?


4. Are there any special rules for Stripe subscriptions we should keep in mind (FTC, refunds, disclosures)?


5. Anything we’re likely to be missing here that’s easy to mess up?



We're trying to do this right but keep it lightweight — especially since we’re not touching payment data from customers.

Would love to hear from anyone who’s done SaaS, worked with GDPR, or handled this kind of setup before.

Thanks in advance!

Didn't sleep, actually, until around 5am. Cried from 11pm to 4 in the morning. Worst decision of my life and I think I made a mistake. Am I even allowed to feel guilty? Was thirteen weeks...second trimester had just started and I ended a life and it's final resting place was my body. I miss my baby. I feel like I should have protected them. Am I normal for this?? Am I stupid to want to celebrate the day they would be due next June? Do I even have the right?

_text_key: missed miscarriage, please help || last week i went in for my first sono, there was no heart beat. i was 9+2 and the baby had stopped growing at 9 weeks. it’s been a full week since the scan and i have yet to have any signs of miscarriage. still feeling very nauseous, no blood. the only thing that might be a sign is that i’ve had some (what i can best describe as) braxton hicks, painless contractions. my d&c is scheduled for thursday and i’m starting to get this sinking thought that “what if the tech was wrong, what if she just missed the heart beat?” listen, i’m typically a very evidence based girly, and i know nine weeks should have produced a heartbeat so i am fairly certain this is just my grief talking. but i don’t know what to do. it feels a little late to ask for another sono and i also don’t know that i can take seeing my baby motionless on a monitor again. if you’ve experienced anything like this, first of all, i’m so sorry, second of all, can you talk me off this ledge? i’m becoming increasingly terrified that i’m about to harm my baby even though i know they aren’t really there any more.

title: Medication Abortion Isn’t Working
body:
Trying to figure out what to do!

I inserted 4 tablets of mifepristone vaginally yesterday around 4:30 pm. I also took 800mg ibuprofen orally at the same time. I had some mild to moderate cramping and light spotting a couple hours later. Then went on through the evening having light cramping and no bleeding. I woke up this morning with some blood in my underwear but not a lot. 

At 10:30 am today I took 1 misoprostol orally followed by 4 more tablets of mifepristone vaginally. I have had mild cramping and a lot of diarrhea since then but no blood at all. 

I feel light headed and nauseous us and just really not myself. I’ve been sipping on water with some herbs like Angelica, black cohosh, blue cohosh, and cotton root bark.  

Now it’s 5:30 and I feel dull cramping in my womb, anxious and fluttering feelings in my heart, and a horrible feeling pit in my stomach. I’ve also felt really emotional and lonely and overwhelmed and kind of just depleted and low capacity this whole time. I can’t make sense of this and can’t figure out what’s happening or what to do. 

I do feel like the dull aches pain is more only right side but it’s not extreme or anything at all. I haven’t taken anything for pain since the initial dose of ibuprofen because there hasn’t been much pain and surely nothing that I felt needed intervention. I’ve been inviting the mild surges of pain that have occurred because I want my cervix to open and my womb to release. 

Sorry if this is all over the place, I’ve not been clear headed and just want to do the right thing and I want this to be over. 

I want to add too: I’ve felt some bouts of chills or feeling cold, really a lot of scattered thoughts and just not feeling myself, a lot of stomach grumbling sounds and frequent bathroom trips, feet and hands falling Adler easily, aches and pains in my whole body but especially lower back and upper back/neck/shoulders. Just overall don’t feel myself and don’t know what to do to help my body release. Also my vagina feels super tender, dry, and irritated and my inner and outer labia feel tender.  

Would appreciate any experience, insight, or advice. 🫶🏼

_text_key: hope is devastating || i am 35 days post misoprostol miscarriage after a blighted ovum and i managed to ovulate on day 25 even with a faintly positive frer that morning. i thought i was having pregnancy symptoms and got faint positives on frer 8 and 9 dpo but they weren’t darkening much and at 10 dpo it was negative. i think it was just residual hcg. i am crushed because i was just started to be happy again and hopeful since i ovulated but it didn’t happen. i wanted to be one of the lucky ones to get pregnant immediately after a mc. i don’t know how to not get my hopes up every cycle and just continue to get crushed when i just want what i lost so badly.
title: Hope is devastating
body:

I thought I was having pregnancy symptoms and got faint positives on FRER 8 and 9 dpo but they weren’t darkening much and at 10 dpo it was negative. I think it was just residual HCG.

I am crushed because I was just started to be happy again and hopeful since I ovulated but it didn’t happen. I wanted to be one of the lucky ones to get pregnant immediately after a MC.
